request.spec:
A steward can clone the sheet to another id (an entry and a button; SHEET_CLONE_MADE to=<id> on this
sheet). The other sheet must be empty (never used); otherwise, or for anyone but a steward, the
clone is refused with an error on the sheet. The clone gets this sheet's today, settings, roles,
rates, holidays, void reasons, templates, people (grades, terms, contacts, aliases, tags, holds,
retirements, patrons), pools, periods (all open) and claims (status, frozen figures, dates, notes,
logs; numbers given afresh in the order the originals were opened (by the sheet's today when each
was opened, then by the order they were added), by the clone's own numbering); statements are not
copied. The clone's first audit line is SHEET_CLONED from=<this sheet's id>, followed by its rollup
lines for every person and its totals.
request.prompt:

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can clone the sheet to another id (an entry and a button; SHEET_CLONE_MADE to=<id> on this
sheet). The other sheet must be empty (never used); otherwise, or for anyone but a steward, the

rates, holidays, void reasons, templates, people (grades, terms, contacts, aliases, tags, holds,
retirements, patrons), pools, periods (all open) and claims (status, frozen figures, dates, notes,
logs; numbers given afresh in the order the originals were opened (by the sheet's today when each
was opened, then by the order they were added), by the clone's own numbering); statements are not
copied. The clone's first audit line is SHEET_CLONED from=<this sheet's id>, followed by its rollup
lines for every person and its totals.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added "clone sheet": a steward can now copy a sheet to a new id. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec, on the first run. Only the first test actually clones a sheet; the other three don't touch the feature.

**What you see:** next to "Archive sheet" there is an id entry (`sheet-clone-to`), a "Clone sheet" button (`sheet-clone`) and a "Cloned to" value (`sheet-cloned-to`). That value is cleared each time the button is pressed and shows the new id once the clone is made. A refusal shows `sheet-error`.

**How it works:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/clone`, refuses (400) anyone but a steward, a blank id, or an id that has ever been used. Otherwise, in one transaction, it copies:
- the sheet's today and its settings, roles, permissions, delegations, rates, holidays, void reasons, templates and tag list;
- people in list order, with their grades, terms, contact, aliases, holds, retirements and patrons;
- pools and their members;
- periods, all reopened;
- claims with their logs and frozen figures, but with anything a statement had fixed cleared.

The copying logic is in `sheet/SheetCloner.java`. I added a general copy-every-matching-row method to the existing `RowCopy` helper for it.

**Audit:** `SHEET_CLONE_MADE … to=<id>` is written on the original sheet. On the clone, `SHEET_CLONED … from=<id>` is written first, then a rollup line for every person and a totals line.

**Claim numbering:** claims that had a number get fresh numbers from the clone's own numbering. The order is by the day each was opened. When that day is the same, claims go person by person in list order, each person's claims in the order they were added. I took that tie-break from what the test expects rather than from the wording. Cam's claim was added first, but the test wants Ada → Ben → Cam, so it can't be a plain sheet-wide "order added". Corrections and splits that point at a renumbered claim are updated to its new number, the same way person transfer already handles it.

**Decisions to check:**
- **Not copied:** statement history, watches, claim comments, claim locks, settle batches and as-of history.
  - I read "notes" in the request as the claim's note field, not its comments. If comments should come across, that's a small addition.
- **Parent link:** I treated the sheet's parent as a setting, so the clone gets the same parent. No test checks this.
- **Archived sheets:** they can still be cloned, because cloning only reads the original. The clone always starts unarchived.
